decisions.reason: Because A stayed on its own page through 2024 and fits the firm’s core platform and data strengths, its apparent performance likely meets aspiration levels well enough that a medium-sized firm in a growing market has little reason to redeploy the resources.

Because C remained on the website after 2024 but lost standalone prominence, its results likely sit closer to the aspiration threshold, yet its close fit with the existing energy-process portfolio and some organizational slack favor keeping it while monitoring performance.

Because E is still offered and supports the firm’s broader integrated platform logic, management is likely to view it as sufficiently useful despite lower visibility and therefore keep it unless forthcoming results clearly fall short of aspirations.
